docRequirement: channels.md:13 binds a channel to being "an MCP server that pushes events into your running Claude Code session, so Claude can react to things that happen while you're not at the terminal", and states exactly one precondition for arrival — "Events only arrive while the session is open" — not that a turn is in flight. The sibling delivery contract at channels-reference.md:256 adds: "Events queue into the session and are processed in order. If several notifications arrive while Claude is busy, they're delivered together on the next turn and Claude handles them as a group." The documented notification is `notifications/claude/channel` with `params.content` (the event body) and `params.meta` (attributes on the emitted `<channel source=...>` tag) — channels-reference.md:229, :238.
current: We ship the channel push path, but it can only steer a turn that is already running, and it steers each event in individually. (1) The subscription itself is TURN-PINNED. `pool.subscribeChannel` has exactly one production call site, inside `armPiPluginPeripherals` — `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` (`managed.mcpChannelUnsubscribe = pool.subscribeChannel(leaserId, ({ text }) => { if (managed.mcpLeaserId !== leaserId) return; canDeliver()?.redirect(text) })`). That method is called only from the send path, `SessionManager.ts:13127` in `getOrCreateAgentUnchecked`, and `disarmPluginPeripherals` (`SessionManager.ts:2381-2387`) removes the listener in `sendMessage`'s finally (`SessionManager.ts:15778`), in `withCapabilityRuntime`'s finally (`:5898`) and in `disposeManagedAgentRuntime` (`:9614`, `:9747`). So between turns there is no subscriber at all: the pool's `dispatchChannelMessage` (`packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:1082-1106`) iterates `this.channelSubscribers.get(leaserId)`, finds an empty set, and the event dies in the pool with no error returned to the pushing server. The field's own comment says so — "Ephemeral claude/channel listener" (`SessionManager.ts:1272-1273`). (2) Even with a listener present, `canDeliver()` (`SessionManager.ts:2399-2405`) returns `undefined` unless BOTH `managed.isProcessing` and `agent.isProcessing?.()` hold, plus a capability-generation match (`:2403`). (3) Delivery is `agent.redirect(text)` — one steer per event into the live turn, raw text, no grouping, no `neutralizeHarnessMarkers` and no `<task-notification>` framing. The machinery that implements the documented discipline exists and is used by the sibling producers: `deliverMonitorEvent` (`SessionManager.ts:2660-2669`) queues into `managed.pendingTaskNotifications` (`:1406`, initialised `:1625`), wakes an idle session, holds pre-first-prompt events as model-only context (`:15101-15109`), flushes one grouped turn at turn end (`:16956-16959`) through `flushPendingTaskNotifications` (`:2677-2698`) and `buildTaskNotificationDelivery` (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/task-notification.ts:53-63`, whose docblock at `:47-52` cites this very channels-reference sentence). Its three producers are `SessionMonitorService` (`:3603`), the cron service (`:2749`) and R10 detached-MCP results (`:18240-18244`); `subscribeChannel` is not one of them. The drop is pinned by a shipped test: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/mcp-channel-gate.test.ts:90-106` ("still drops a push when no turn is in flight", enabled policy + idle session, expects `redirected` to be `[]`). Separately, nothing is delivered at all on a stock install: `getMcpChannelPushEnabled()` (`packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:1149-1155`) defaults to `false` (`storage.ts:183`), so `resolveChannelPolicy()` (`SessionManager.ts:2552-2554`) yields `enabled: false` and `applyChannelPolicy` (`mcp-pool.ts:757-770`) installs no dispatcher.
divergence: Two deltas, both in delivery semantics of a feature we do ship — not absence. (a) IDLE ARRIVAL IS NOT SUPPORTED. The doc's only precondition is that the session is open; ours is that a turn is in flight. And the cause is one layer deeper than the `canDeliver()` gate the finding cites: the subscription is created and destroyed with the turn, so an event arriving between turns has no listener to reach and is discarded inside `McpClientPool.dispatchChannelMessage` before any session-level gate runs. Fixing only `canDeliver` would change nothing. (b) NO GROUPING. Several events during a busy turn are each `redirect()`-ed into the running turn immediately, where the contract is one grouped delivery in arrival order on the NEXT turn. Note what is NOT wrong: the policy/gate layer (`ChannelPolicy`, `resolveManagedChannelPolicy`, fail-closed default) is correct and deliberate, and the grouped-delivery machinery already exists — this is a wiring gap between `pool.subscribeChannel` and `deliverMonitorEvent`, plus a lifetime change on the subscription. Adjacent and NOT part of this delta (it gates any live verification): our client reads `params.text` (`packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:357-361`) while the documented field is `params.content`, and we never emit the `<channel source=... >` wrapper or `meta` attributes.

change.what: Move the channel subscription off the turn. Add `private ensureSessionChannelSubscription(managed: ManagedSession): void` modelled on `ensurePluginCommandMonitors` (`:2468`, the existing session-lifetime peripheral that is deliberately never disarmed per turn): subscribe once per `mcpLeaserId`, re-subscribing only when the leaser identity changes, and store the disposer in a renamed field (see below). Call it from `getOrCreateAgentUnchecked` right after the pool handles are published (`:13121-13124`), and keep `pool.setChannelPolicy(this.resolveChannelPolicy())` re-applied per capability generation where it is today (`:2435`) so a policy narrowing still lands immediately. Remove the `mcpChannelUnsubscribe` lines from `disarmPluginPeripherals` (`:2382-2384`) — that method must keep disarming `pluginMonitorServices` only — and tear the channel subscription down where the MCP lease is released, in `disposeManagedAgentRuntime` (`:9605-9614`), beside `stopPluginCommandMonitors`. Drop the capability-generation pin for this path: a channel push is not turn-pinned work, so it must not be silenced by `canDeliver`'s `:2403` check. Keep the leaser-identity guard `if (managed.mcpLeaserId !== leaserId) return`.

Replace `canDeliver()?.redirect(text)` with a route into the existing discipline, the same shape R10 already uses at `:18240-18244`: `void this.deliverMonitorEvent({ sessionKey: { workspaceId: managed.workspace.id, sessionId: managed.id }, taskId: `channel:${server}`, text })` (destructure `server` as well as `text` from the `McpChannelMessage`). That one call buys all three documented rules at once — idle wake, one grouped delivery in arrival order on the next turn, pre-first-prompt hold as model-only context — plus the `neutralizeHarnessMarkers` framing from `buildTaskNotificationDelivery`, which the raw `redirect(text)` path does not have today.

Rename the field to reflect its new lifetime (e.g. `mcpChannelSubscription?: { leaserId: string; dispose: () => void }`) and rewrite the comment: it is no longer "Ephemeral … always removed before the MCP lease" per turn, it is session-scoped and released with the lease. In the `deliverMonitorEvent` docblock, rule 1 currently names `armPiPluginPeripherals` as "the other out-of-turn producer … can only steer a LIVE turn, so an event arriving between turns was dropped outright" (`:2649-2651`) — that sentence becomes false; make channel push a listed producer instead.

blastRadius: One production subscriber (`SessionManager.ts:2436`), so the code fan-out is small — but the delivery mechanism changes class, and that is the risk. Today a channel event is an `agent.redirect()` steer: transient, not a transcript entry, and it cannot start work. After the fix it goes through `sendMessage` (`flushPendingTaskNotifications`, `:2682-2692`), which PERSISTS a turn to the session transcript and can start a model turn while nobody is at the machine — a persistence boundary and a spend boundary, i.e. a risk trigger in this repo, and exactly why `2026-07-26-sandbox-and-managed-policy.md:104-106` called the drop "the only thing making the current no-gate state survivable". The fail-closed layers must stay untouched: `mcpChannelPushEnabled` default `false` (`packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:183`, `:1149-1155`), `resolveManagedChannelPolicy` deny-terminal, `applyChannelPolicy` install-time gate (`packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:757-770`), and the renderer toggle (`apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/settings/PermissionsSettingsPage.tsx:256-262`). Shared state: `managed.pendingTaskNotifications` (`:1406`) gains a third producer alongside monitor events, cron and R10 detached results — ordering is by arrival, which is what the doc asks for, and the queue is runtime-only and deliberately not persisted (`:1398-1405`), so no stored-shape migration. Tests that read this wiring: `__tests__/mcp-channel-gate.test.ts`, `SessionManager.process-supervisor.test.ts:967`, `__tests__/monitor-idle-wake.test.ts`, `__tests__/mcp-task-notification-routing.test.ts`, `__tests__/managed-sandbox-and-channel.test.ts` (policy keys only), `packages/shared/tests/mcp-pool.test.ts:705-786` (pool-level subscribe, unaffected). No RPC/wire change: `McpChannelMessage` (`packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:102-105`) and the `permissions:getMcpChannelPush` / `setMcpChannelPush` channels are untouched. Imported-plugin path: a Claude channel plugin installed through the adapters reaches this same pool subscription, so any behaviour here is what an imported `claude-plugins-official` channel gets.
userImpact: None observable on a stock install: the switch is off by default, so no dispatcher is installed and no server can push at all. Two steps surface it. (1) Settings → Permissions → "Allow MCP servers to interject" (`PermissionsSettingsPage.tsx:256-262`). (2) Connect an MCP server that sends `notifications/claude/channel` with `params.text`. Then the page's headline scenario fails exactly as advertised-not-to: the user walks away, CI or a chat bridge posts an event, and nothing happens — no turn starts, no notification appears, and the pushing server gets no error back, because the event is discarded inside the pool with no listener present. It appears to work only if the user happens to be mid-turn, and then it is injected as a raw steer into whatever the agent was already doing, one steer per event, rather than as a grouped, framed background notification on the next turn. For a spec-conformant channel plugin the fix alone is still not user-visible, because our client reads `params.text` while the documented field is `params.content` — that key mismatch has to be closed too before a live channel smoke can pass.
